text: 🇲🇽⚽ The world wants to come to Mexico. She named where the warmth comes from. "The warmth every visitor felt — that doesn't come from the conquest, nor from eurocentrism. It comes from the indigenous peoples." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on World Cup 2026 "The whole world wants to come to Mexico," she said of the tourists arriving for the 2026 World Cup.

🇲🇽🎨 Superior beings and inferior beings — the vision she refuses. "If we keep carrying that vision that there are superior beings and inferior beings, that we all have only one identity and there is no pluriculturality, then we will keep promoting racism and classism." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on eurocentrism She tied it to the new Indigenous Law and Article 2's recognition of Mexico as a pluricultural nation.

🇲🇽🌎 She told the King of Spain what matters more than an apology. "Beyond the apology, what matters most for Mexico is the identity it represents for all Mexicans — the recognition of the peoples." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on her message to King Felipe VI Mexico still awaits Spain's apology for the abuses of the Conquest. After 300 years of colonial rule and 200 of independence, she noted, 20% of the population still identifies as indigenous.

🇲🇽⚖️ “200 years of the Mexican state — and we have never had an Indigenous Law.” "Two hundred years of the Mexican state's existence, and we have never had an Indigenous Law." — Adelfo Regino Montes, director of INPI The government opened national consultation on the General Law of the Rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Peoples, grounded in the Article 2 reform of Sept 30, 2024. It covers 69 indigenous peoples, one Afro-Mexican people and 16,728 communities, and reaches Congress on Oct 12 — Day of Indigenous Resistance.

🚨🇲🇽 The “paper of record” ran a story sourced to no one. "How can a story like this run in a newspaper that calls itself one of the best in the world?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the NYT report On June 28 the New York Times claimed, citing unnamed sources, that Morena officials had become informants for the US government in drug-trafficking cases. Mexico has no information that anyone is cooperating with Washington, Sheinbaum said. Sonora Governor Rubén Rocha sent the paper a letter denying he is under any US investigation.

🇲🇽✊ MEXICO OPENS ITS FIRST INDIGENOUS RIGHTS LAW IN 200 YEARS

President Sheinbaum signed the call today for a national consultation to build Mexico's first General Law on the Rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Peoples — two centuries after the Mexican state was founded. It will consult 69 indigenous peoples and one Afro-Mexican people across more than 16,000 communities, some 8 million people — 20.5% of the population — through 82 regional assemblies before the initiative reaches Congress on October 12. Each community deliberates under its own normative systems, not a decree handed down from above.

🇲🇽🇪🇸 SPAIN'S KING CAME TO MEXICO — AND THE TERMS HAD CHANGED

King Felipe VI met President Sheinbaum at Palacio Nacional — the first meeting between a Spanish monarch and a Mexican head of state since AMLO froze ties over Madrid's refusal to apologize for the conquest. The thaw came only after Felipe VI publicly acknowledged there was "much abuse" during the conquest. Mexico never dropped the demand; Spain moved toward it.

🌽🇲🇽 MEXICO PROJECTED TO STAY THE WORLD'S #1 CORN IMPORTER THROUGH 2035

A new OECD–FAO outlook projects Mexico will absorb 10% of all global corn imports by 2035 — the single largest share on the planet, ahead of the EU (9%), Vietnam (8%), Japan (7%) and China (3%). The overwhelming majority comes from the United States. This is exactly why the Fourth Transformation's push for food sovereignty — and AMLO's fight to keep US GM corn out of the tortilla — was never just symbolism.

🚨🇲🇽 TELECOM GIANTS LEGALLY REQUIRED TO DESTROY CUSTOMERS' BIOMETRIC DATA

As Mexico's mobile-line registry deadline hits June 30, operators Telcel, AT&T, Movistar and Altán Redes are legally required to destroy the biometric data they collected from customers linking their lines to the CURP — it was for identity verification only, not a database to keep. The catch, per the Mexican Internet Association: the companies "neither inform nor provide evidence" that they aren't holding on to it. Your biometrics aren't a corporate asset, and Mexicans are right to demand proof.
